correctness.rationale: For each binary residue after e digits, the exact residual is F_(floor((c+r)/2^e),popcount((c+r) mod 2^e) mod m). A two-interval argument exhausts reachable parameters and the high-depth tail. Every parameter pair denotes a different function: unequal phases at the same offset differ immediately; for offsets a<a prime, evaluate at n=2^h-a prime, obtaining a digit-sum difference h-popcount(a prime-a-1)-1, not constant modulo m as h varies. These lemmas establish the infinite exact count and the power-of-two specialization. The standalone checker independently confirmed all 903 shift/modulus BFS and minimization cases, 2047 popcount extrema, 96 power-shift specializations and 30600 residual identities. Bounded computations are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: The natural family of generalized Thue–Morse digit-sum words has a complete exact descriptional-complexity invariant under every nonnegative translation and every alphabet modulus, including explicit minimal reachable states and transition functions. The power-of-two family displays a sharp transition between triangular and linear growth as the modulus varies, a structural result not obtained from generic existence bounds. It supplies an interpretable benchmark for automata minimization and k-kernel calculations, rather than an arbitrary finite cutoff or recomputation of known tables.
